newsitem.title: GERMANY: Moulinex sees flat Euro appliance market.
newsitem.headline: Moulinex sees flat Euro appliance market.

text.p: Moulinex chairman Pierre Blayau said the European appliance market would likely be stable this year even though the German and French markets are expected to remain weak.

"The market in France and Germany will not be good. However, it'll be slightly better in Britain. Italy and Spain should be steady or slightly weaker," he told a news conference at the Domotechnica appliance show in Cologne.
He reiterated that he expected flat turnover for the 1996/97 year ending on March 31, compared with 7.8 billion francs in the previous year, and a slight improvement in operating results.
The group signed an accord last month with five unions on a restructuring plan envisaging 2,600 job cuts -- 2,100 of them in France and 500 in Germany -- and two plant closures.
Blayau reiterated that the first "tangible" signs of the restructuring would be felt in the 1997/98 fiscal year.

"Our goal is to maintain our market share in France and Germany," he said, adding that the group sought to expand in North and South America, Asia and Russia. It expects higher turnover growth outside Europe.
It has nine percent of the U.S. market, where its Krups coffee making and Moulinex appliance brands are successful, and hopes to raise that to 12 percent.
"The Americans are very sensitive to the aesthetics of our products," he said at the show, where Moulinex presented nearly a dozen new products with smooth forms and rounded lines.
New products are expected to account for between 25 and 30 percent of sales from here on, the company said.
In terms of sales, it ranks fourth internationally and is market leader in Germany.
Most of the Moulinex products sold in the United States are produced at its Mexican plant which employs 900 people.
The group would like to find an Asian partner. It is in talks in China that could lead to some kind of venture agreement before the summer, Blayau said.
